adjust.agentBrief:
You are the triage agent. Do not change the repository: no edits, commits, or pushes. The issue is below. Read it, the repository's own guidance (such as AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md), and the code it touches, then decide whether the issue is ready for a spec. Do not write the spec; a spec agent does that after you, and only when your outcome lets it.

When the evidence sits between two outcomes, choose the more cautious one. Do not choose `ready to implement` just because a fix looks easy; check the code first.

Write only {triage}, following this template. When there are questions, make `## Open questions` the first `##` section and number them `1.`, `2.`, …, without an outcome prefix. Omit the section when there are no questions:

# <title>

## Open questions
1. The smallest set of concrete questions that would unblock it.

## Reason
<one paragraph: the reason for your outcome>

## Notes for the spec
(ready to implement, ready to spec) The code involved, the approaches you saw, and the risks.

Leave out empty sections.

prose.exampleNote: Illustrative only: the spec key and paths are examples, not exact storage paths. Not every belt has a Spec stage.
prose.introduction: Beltline replaces recognised {name} tokens when preparing an agent's brief. Output placeholders insert paths, not file contents. The issue or other subject, any note and the outcome footer are added automatically.
prose.resolution: A stage's placeholder is the key chosen on that stage. Briefs use that key and the fixed names. A stage id or agent id is not another name for the output unless it is also the chosen key. A key used on mutually exclusive routes is the output of the route this run took, including after the routes join, and never another route's output. Going back into a fork keeps the outputs its stages already wrote until they write again. The current stage's own key is this attempt's output path. Another stage's key is that stage's latest finished output. With no finished output, the brief shows (no <filename> yet). When no route has selected one writer, it shows (no <key> output yet). These markers are not files in the checkout. Fixed names keep their own meanings and cannot be stage keys.
prose.resolutionNote: A stage key is that stage's output on the route this run took. The current stage's own key is this attempt's file. Going back into a fork keeps the outputs already written there until they are written again. A missing output reads (no <filename> yet), and a key no route has selected reads (no <key> output yet). Fixed names keep their meanings.
prose.syntax: The name check recognises nonempty lowercase letters, digits, - and _. {}, {Draft} and JSON-like braces are not names for that check. Fenced code is ignored by validation; inline code is checked. Fences do not escape rendering: recognised tokens are still replaced there. Fenced {artifacts} alone does not request instructions. Unknown tokens in an existing brief remain literal text.
prose.warnings: Belt Save checks effective briefs: a stage override, otherwise its pinned agent's brief. It accepts fixed names and the placeholder keys chosen on this belt's stages. The same key may be used on fork routes that a run cannot take together. Unknown names are warned as text and keep their literal spelling. A belt saved before stages had their own keys converts missing keys from the originally pinned agents; a brief that used a stage id must be corrected to use the chosen key. Renaming a stage key does not rewrite brief tokens.
